items.text: England & Wales and Northern Ireland censuses were 21 March 2021. Scotland’s Census was 20 March 2022. A UK-wide 2021 census map would be a date mismatch for Scotland.

UK-born is the four UK countries as published. NISRA MS-A16 note 3: ‘Europe: Other non-EU’ includes United Kingdom (part not specified) and Ireland (part not specified) — those cells are not added into UK-born here. NRS vital-events United Kingdom rows can include Crown Dependencies (see table notes).

E&W 2021 high-level White includes White British, White Irish, Gypsy or Irish Traveller, Roma, and Other White. Scotland’s form also puts Irish, Polish, Gypsy/Traveller, Roma, Showman/Showwoman and Other White under the White heading — but NRS also publishes a ‘minority ethnic’ figure that includes those White minorities. NISRA lists Irish Traveller and Roma as separate columns from White. These three White percentages are not the same category.

Scotland’s 2022 high-level tick-box groups treat African as its own heading and Chinese as a named Asian group. E&W 2021 presents a five-group roll-up (White / Mixed / Asian / Black / Other). NISRA MS-B01 uses a different intermediate list (Indian, Chinese, Filipino, Pakistani, Black African, …). Groups are shown as published, not forced onto one UK list.

Modern affiliation starts in 2001. The question is voluntary. Scotland does not impute a religion when the question is skipped — ‘Not stated’ is a valid residual (6.2% in 2022). E&W 2021 has a different non-response treatment. Northern Ireland publishes current religion (MS-B19) and a separate ‘religion or religion brought up in’ table (MS-B23). MS-B23 is not mixed into the E&W/Scotland affiliation percentages. MS-B19 has no standalone Muslim column (Muslim is inside Other religions).

APS Table 2.1 is self-reported citizenship (British / non-British). Scotland Figure 9 and NISRA MS-B15 are national identity (feeling of attachment), not passports and not citizenship. They are never written onto the nationality stock layer.

items.text: England & Wales and Northern Ireland censuses were 21 March 2021. Scotland’s Census was 20 March 2022. A UK-wide 2021 census map would be a date mismatch for Scotland.

UK-born is the four UK countries as published. NISRA MS-A16 note 3: ‘Europe: Other non-EU’ includes United Kingdom (part not specified) and Ireland (part not specified) — those cells are not added into UK-born here. NRS vital-events United Kingdom rows can include Crown Dependencies (see table notes).

E&W 2021 high-level White includes White British, White Irish, Gypsy or Irish Traveller, Roma, and Other White. Scotland’s form also puts Irish, Polish, Gypsy/Traveller, Roma, Showman/Showwoman and Other White under the White heading — but NRS also publishes a ‘minority ethnic’ figure that includes those White minorities. NISRA lists Irish Traveller and Roma as separate columns from White. These three White percentages are not the same category.

Scotland’s 2022 high-level tick-box groups treat African as its own heading and Chinese as a named Asian group. E&W 2021 presents a five-group roll-up (White / Mixed / Asian / Black / Other). NISRA MS-B01 uses a different intermediate list (Indian, Chinese, Filipino, Pakistani, Black African, …). Groups are shown as published, not forced onto one UK list.

Modern affiliation starts in 2001. The question is voluntary. Scotland does not impute a religion when the question is skipped — ‘Not stated’ is a valid residual (6.2% in 2022). E&W 2021 has a different non-response treatment. Northern Ireland publishes current religion (MS-B19) and a separate ‘religion or religion brought up in’ table (MS-B23). MS-B23 is not mixed into the E&W/Scotland affiliation percentages. MS-B19 has no standalone Muslim column (Muslim is inside Other religions).

APS Table 2.1 is self-reported citizenship (British / non-British). Scotland Figure 9 and NISRA MS-B15 are national identity (feeling of attachment), not passports and not citizenship. They are never written onto the nationality stock layer.

nation.reason: Contested model results — not a mapped official series.

notes: There is no official mapped ‘cost of immigration’. The assumption controls filter published estimates — they do not compute a new true net figure.
Static annual snapshots, lifetime NPVs, and OBR age-profile scenarios can differ in sign depending on the visa route, dependants, public-goods allocation, and time window.

methods.name: OBR FRS / EFO
methods.frame: Age-specific tax and spend profiles applied to population projections with net-migration variants. Sensitive to the ONS long-run migration settle and to assumed earnings/length of stay. Usually a debt-path scenario, not a £ per migrant.

methods.name: MAC 2025 lifetime / static
methods.frame: Cohort and visa-route model (Skilled Worker, Health & Care, dependants, Partner route). Discount rate (~3%) and lifetime assumptions drive NPV. Not the whole stock.

methods.name: Dustmann–Frattini 2014
methods.frame: Static period accounting ~1995–2011/12, EEA vs non-EEA. Foundational in debate; not official statistics and not current. The 2013 discussion paper quotes different totals for the same window.

methods.name: Migration Observatory briefing
methods.frame: Secondary synthesis (23 June 2026). Table 1 is the reason estimates disagree: children, public goods, recent vs all-resident, and year all move the sign.

assumptionAxes.label: Time frame
assumptionAxes.help: Static studies add up one year or a historical window. Dynamic studies project a lifetime NPV. They are not the same question.

assumptionAxes.label: Average vs marginal
assumptionAxes.help: Average allocates a share of existing public goods to every person. Marginal asks what extra spending an extra person causes. MAC Table 11 varies this.

assumptionAxes.label: Public goods counted
assumptionAxes.help: Defence, debt interest and ‘pure’ public goods are the usual disagreement. MAC Table 11 reports Pure public goods MC=0 and Congestible public goods MC=0 as sensitivities on the same 2022/23 groups.

assumptionAxes.label: Who is counted
assumptionAxes.help: Whole-stock EEA/non-EEA totals, recent arrivals, and visa-route cohorts answer different questions. They must not be added together.
